diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: Ebrahim Azizi, head of the National Security Commission of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, called the orders of Mojtaba Khamenei, leader of the Islamic Republic, "final" and said they will respond to any threat immediately and more harshly than before. Azizi added that they determine the end of the war, not the losers of the 12-day and 40-day wars. The leader's media reported that Mojtaba Khamenei emphasized that any level and type of threat must be met with an immediate and impactful response without geographical limitation.

Ali Nikzad, the deputy speaker of the parliament, said in a speech before the session on Sunday, 10 Aban, that the window for nuclear negotiations is now closed to the enemy because they have nothing new to offer Iran. He warned that if the enemies commit another aggression, the remaining windows might also be closed and emphasized that the wisest action is to accept the realities and unconditionally implement the seven conditions of the Islamic Republic. Nikzad added that if the enemies repeat their mistake, as emphasized in yesterday's meeting of Khamenei with senior military commanders, they will face an immediate, effective, and geographically unrestricted response.

Rouhollah Rahimpour, a political analyst, referred to the report of a call between Trump and Netanyahu and said that if the war resumes, the likelihood of it starting a few days after the US midterm elections is higher, and the military and nuclear infrastructure of the Islamic Republic will be prioritized in potential attacks.

On the early morning of Sunday, 10 Aban, the execution sentence of a prisoner named Iman Ashraf was carried out in Adelabad Prison in Shiraz. The prisoner had previously been sentenced to death for murder. This news was reported by the HRANA news agency.
Hakan Fidan, Turkey's foreign minister, warned that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, by disrupting energy supply and international trade, has increased pressure on the global economy.

Qatar Gas Transport Company "Nakilat" announced that a liquefied natural gas carrier named "Al Mayeda" was attacked by "unknown objects" on Friday evening while moving in the Persian Gulf. The company added that none of the crew were injured and the incident had no environmental impact. The ship is in a safe condition and the assessment of the consequences of the incident is ongoing.
Videos received by Iran International show that a group of Iranians residing in the UK commemorated Cyrus the Great and the Pahlavi kings on Saturday, 9 Aban.
The police commander of Abadan reported the closure of a clothing store in the city due to the installation of obscene and satanic signs.

Nasrollah Pejmanfar, head of the Parliament's Article 90 Commission, stated in a public session on Sunday, November 1, 2026, that the issue of withdrawing from the NPT should be seriously on the agenda, expressing hope that this decision would be made in obedience to Mojtaba Khamenei. Pejmanfar said he hopes this decision will come to fruition and that everyone will decide, in obedience to the leadership, to withdraw from the NPT to make them understand that Iran will not back down in the face of these pressures. He added that every time Grossi and the NPT team entered Iran, the country suffered significant damage and harm.
Videos received show a group of retired steelworkers in Isfahan gathered on Sunday, 10 Aban, protesting livelihood problems and shouted: "Our enemy is right here, they lie that it is America."

Peyvand and Borna Naeimi, Baha'i citizens imprisoned in Kerman prison, were sentenced to imprisonment by the fifth branch of the Revolutionary Court of this city. Peyvand Naeimi was sentenced to 12 years, six months, and one day, and Borna Naeimi to eight years in prison.

The International Testing Agency announced that Poneh Akhoundtabar Mazandarani, known as Tina Akhoundtabar, has been banned from sports competitions for three years due to a positive doping test and admission of the violation. The sample taken from her on December 6, 2024, during the "Boxing Champions Night" competition in Dubai contained the prohibited substance clenbuterol. The ban starts on February 20, 2025, and lasts until February 19, 2028, and her results in these competitions have been annulled.

Afrooz Eslam Panah, the mother of the late Behboud Hassanzadeh, passed away on 8 Aban. Behboud Hassanzadeh was 37 years old, held a master's degree in law, and was the father of two daughters. Behboud was killed by a war bullet on 18 Dey 404 in Kouhchenar, Fars, while helping one of the wounded.

Hossein Samsami, a member of the Parliament's Economic Commission, said that the currency for essential goods is increasing by 1,000 tomans daily and that the country's economic conditions will worsen within a month. He added that the Ministry of Industry, Mine and Trade sent a letter to the Central Bank to supply only a few items at the rate of 188,000 tomans, while other goods will be supplied near the free market rate. Samsami warned that the prices of more than four thousand goods will deliberately increase by 100,000 tomans and that prices of goods and cars will rise by 40 to 50 percent in the next one or two months.

Israel's Channel 12 reported on Sunday, November 1, 2026, that signs of a potential resumption of war with Iran are increasing daily. Raz Zimet, head of the Iran program at Israel's Institute for National Security Studies, told the channel that in his opinion, only a few days or at most a few weeks remain until Trump concludes that waiting for Iran's response is futile. Zimet also estimated that the Islamic Republic currently possesses about 1,500 ballistic missiles, and in the event of another confrontation, Israeli cities would again be targeted by these missiles.
A video published on social media shows a baker calling the rationed flour sent to him "low quality" and saying, "This flour is weak and cannot be used to bake bread."

Various cities in France witnessed protests on the evening of Saturday, 9 Aban, against rising living costs and declining quality of public services. These gatherings had fewer participants and limited violence compared to previous weeks. Students, trade union members, and fewer yellow vest protesters demonstrated against fuel price hikes, inflation, and the policies of Emmanuel Macron's government.

Mohammad Akraminia, spokesperson for the Islamic Republic Army, said Iran is fully prepared to respond to the US even outside West Asia and that Iran controls the timing of any potential future war's end. He warned that any renewed US aggression will face an immediate and broader response and added that US facilities and interests anywhere could be targeted. He also emphasized that the future war could be longer and the US president will not be able to determine its end time.

The news website Ynet reported that the Israeli army has completed its preparations for a new round of conflict with the Islamic Republic, and the start of operations depends on the decision of Donald Trump, the President of the United States. Political and military coordination between Israel and the US continues, and Benjamin Netanyahu, the Prime Minister of Israel, has reviewed operational scenarios in various meetings.

Today, Sunday 10 Aban, a group of retired steel industry workers in Isfahan held a protest gathering in the city. The protest was against the performance of the supplementary insurance "Dana", issues related to medical services, incomplete implementation of salary adjustments, and other livelihood demands of these citizens.

Today, Sunday, a group of Social Security retirees protested in front of the organization's buildings in the cities of Shush and Ahvaz. Their demands include improving living conditions, increasing salaries and purchasing power, controlling inflation and price hikes, creating job opportunities, reducing housing rents, and access to free education, healthcare, and social services.

Esmail Kowsari, a member of the Parliament's National Security Commission, said that until the seven clauses announced by the Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council are implemented, they will not enter negotiations with Washington. He added that at this stage, they cannot easily accept negotiations and until these conditions are operational, there will be no negotiations with the Americans. Kowsari also said that Americans have not adhered to their commitments in previous negotiations, and for this reason, they are not optimistic about the US.

Mehrdad Akhlaghi, the Minister of Defense of the Islamic Republic, announced that the ministry is pursuing the enhancement of intelligent combat readiness and the implementation of a strategy for immediate, effective, and proportionate response to any threat. He also mentioned accelerating the design, production, and supply cycle of defense equipment and strengthening industrial and technological infrastructure. Akhlaghi emphasized that any aggression will be met with a proportionate and decisive response and that the Islamic Republic will not be caught off guard by threats.

Portuguese riot police attacked protesters with batons and shields early Sunday morning, November 1, in Rossio Square in central Lisbon and dismantled their tent camp. The camp had been set up in protest against the housing crisis. After the police intervention, protesters dispersed in the historic city center streets and created barriers using available materials.

According to videos received by Iran International, a group of Iranians residing in Norway held a ceremony commemorating Cyrus the Great in the city of Stavanger on Saturday, 9 Aban, and honored the memory of the immortal figures of the national revolution.

Mohammad Sadegh Rezaei, head of Mazandaran University of Medical Sciences, reported a shortage of ambulances in the province and said that supplying 160 ambulances is essential for the complete renovation of Mazandaran's emergency fleet. The head of pre-hospital emergency services in Mazandaran also emphasized the need to increase the number of emergency bases and strengthen the rescue fleet due to the province's fixed and floating population and the high volume of traffic accidents.

Abdulrahman Dorostaran, a citizen from Rask and brother of Omar Dorostaran, a politically executed accused, has been detained by intelligence officers for three weeks and is currently held in a security detention center in Zahedan.

Amnesty International reports that the international community's silence on widespread killings in Iran, along with ongoing impunity, has paved the way for a cycle of violence. Amnesty International emphasizes that the killings in Dey 1404 show the same signs of crimes against humanity as the 1401 crackdown. The organization sees breaking this cycle requires holding the commanders and perpetrators accountable by the international community.

Rahimian Hospital in Alvand city, the only active hospital in Alborz county of Qazvin province, lacks an independent ambulance. Reza Darvishvand, CEO of the hospital's charity, stated that in severe patient conditions, an ambulance must be dispatched from Qazvin or the patient must be transferred to medical centers by private vehicle. This process sometimes takes about 40 minutes and can endanger patients' health.
A sandstorm swept through Haftkel city in Khuzestan province on Sunday, 10 Aban, covering the sky of the city with thick dust.

Reports indicate that various costs are being imposed on families in public schools. It was reported that a public school charged 5 million tomans in tuition but lacks facilities, and schools take money from parents under various pretexts. It was also reported that public schools even pass on water, electricity, and gas bills to parents.
Today, Zahed Seyed Karimi, a citizen from the village of Bab Khaledabad in Oshnavieh, was reportedly arrested by IRGC intelligence agents and transferred to an unknown location.

Mohammad Mo'tamedizadeh, a member of the presidium of the Article 90 Commission of the Parliament, said any country that initiates aggression against Iran should know it will face a decisive response from the Islamic Republic. He also added that any cooperation with the enemy, whether in regional countries or elsewhere in the world, that threatens Iran's national interests will face a decisive response. Mo'tamedizadeh defined the enemy as anyone directly or indirectly involved in aggression against the country or who has allowed their land to be used by Iran's enemies.

Today, Sunday 10 Aban, a number of Social Security retirees held a protest in front of the organization's buildings in Kermanshah and Tehran. The protesting retirees stated that addressing livelihood and medical issues are among their demands.

Raheleh Soltani was sent to prison to serve her sentence. Raheleh Soltani, a resident of Maaf village in Bandar Anzali, Gilan province, was sent to prison on Saturday, 9 Aban to serve her sentence. She had previously been sentenced to five months in prison for contacting a foreign media outlet and protesting the price increase of her mother's medicines.

Ali-Asghar Bagherzadeh, Babolsar representative in parliament, said in his speech on 10 Aban that national resilience alongside defense power determines the country's fate in wartime. He added resilience is not created by orders but by trust, which arises from justice, honesty, and the results of correct decisions. Bagherzadeh also said the government can take measures to increase social capital and public trust without imposing new financial burdens.
Videos received by Iran International show that a group of Iranians residing in Australia circulated the Lion and Sun flags with their cars in the city of Adelaide on Saturday, 9 Aban.

Today, a group of Social Security retirees held a protest in front of the Social Security Organization buildings in Rasht and Dezful. These retirees demanded attention to their medical and livelihood problems. Also, in Rasht, these retirees protested against death sentences by chanting slogans.

Five detainees from the January 2026 protests named Shahab Zahdi, Amir Reza Rezaei, Vahid Ghahremani, Emran Amani, and a cleric named Mehdi have been sentenced to death. The death sentence of Mohammad Naderi, a political prisoner, has also been confirmed by the Supreme Court. These individuals were sentenced in connection with cases including the arson of a Basij base and charges related to Israel.

Reuters reported, quoting an informed official, that negotiators of the Islamic Republic of Iran are talking with Qatari mediators in Doha for the third consecutive day. The goal of these talks has been announced as an effort to reach an agreement to end the war between the US and Iran.

Mehdi Taj, president of the Iranian Football Federation, expressed hope that the Iran under-23 team could qualify for the Olympics after years of failure during the introduction ceremony of Yahya Golmohammadi as the new head coach. Taj praised the selection of Golmohammadi, stating that he and Amir Ghalenoei have won 18 championship titles combined and are among the best coaches in the country. He also pointed to the capacity of young players in the Premier League, noting that 48 players under 21 play in the league and they are the target market for Golmohammadi and his colleagues.

The police commander of Chaldoran county reported the arrest of the operator of an Instagram page about dating in this county. This individual was arrested on charges of promoting immorality and publishing criminal content, and their Instagram page has been blocked.

The government has increased the price of wheat used by macaroni factories by more than two and a half times since the beginning of Aban; this decision raises the production costs of macaroni and industrial bread. Mahtab Gholizadeh, an economic journalist, explains the government's currency policies in the pricing of industrial flour.

Messages received by Iran International indicate increasing economic pressure on citizens. Some audience members reported inability to provide basic needs, including food, stationery, and clothing for their children. Others mentioned severe sales decline, delayed salaries, and difficulties in paying rent.

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, said there has been no meeting with the American delegation nor has one been planned. He added that the Iranian delegation's trip to Qatar was to continue contacts and consultations with Qatari intermediaries. Araghchi also said negotiations about their seven-day plan, now reduced to a two-day plan, are ongoing and no definitive result has been reached yet.
It was reported that Elyas Ghanavati Lari, a writer from Mahshahr, was arrested by security forces 12 days ago on 29 Mehr and remains in detention.
Videos released show that a group of retirees in Kermanshah and Ahvaz gathered on Sunday, 10 Aban, to protest economic problems and shouted "Enough warmongering, our tables are empty."

Mohammad Taghi Naqdali, representative of Khomeinishahr in parliament, said in his mid-session speech on Sunday, 10 Aban, that people are under the most severe economic pressures and the government's weak actions are not worthy of the Ummah. He added that the government continues the policy of price increases, from internet, electricity, and water to other goods, only moving towards higher prices. Naqdali also said that if he were the speaker of the parliament, he would suspend all orders, and the parliament's score with the people is zero because they do not feel that any work is being done for their livelihood.

Iman Rashidi, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Yazd, returned to Yazd prison on Saturday, 9 Aban, after the end of his leave period. According to Harana News Agency, he had previously been granted leave from this prison.

Swiss police used water cannons, tear gas, and plastic bullets early Sunday, 10 Aban, to disperse protesters in central Zurich. Several hundred people gathered following calls on social media for protests similar to recent ones in France and other countries. Police reported masked protesters placed trash bins and other objects in the street and set fires, and that fireworks, bottles, and stones were thrown at emergency forces, damaging some shops and public transport stations.

Videos received by Iran International show the burial ceremony of Abolfazl Nejadfathi in Shushtar County on Sunday, 3 Aban. According to received reports, this young man was shot dead by officers at a checkpoint in the beltway area of Shushtar city on Friday, 1 Aban.

Reports received by Iran International indicate that families in many public schools are forced to pay costs related even to the provision of the most basic school facilities. Citizens say school administrators charge students for everything from exam paper fees to water and electricity bills of the school.

Saeed Tavakoli, CEO of the National Iranian Gas Company, announced that this year there is about a 130 million cubic meter reduction in gas capacity, and the total reduction and shortage of gas at peak consumption reaches about 400 million cubic meters. He mentioned that damage to the facilities of four refineries during the 40-day war caused a loss of 230 million cubic meters of capacity, of which 100 million cubic meters have been restored. In previous years, the gas shortage at peak consumption was about 250 to 300 million cubic meters.
A video received by Iran International shows that a group of Iranians living in Spain gathered on Sunday, 10 Aban, in the city of Barcelona to protest the executions by the Islamic Republic.

A widespread wave of protests continues in Europe, and on Saturday, October 31, hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets in seven countries. Protesters demanded increased funding for schools and social services, reduced living costs, and the cancellation of mandatory military service.

Mohammad Mokhber, assistant to Mojtaba Khamenei, wrote on X on Sunday, 10 Aban, that the Islamic Republic's defense doctrine is rapidly evolving and the geography of threat no longer determines the geography of response. Mokhber added that the redefinition of deterrence scope has gone beyond the regional framework and the origin, extent, and location of the threat do not limit Iran's deterrence calculations. It was also announced on Saturday, 9 Aban, that any threat against the Iranian government will be met with an immediate, effective, and geographically unlimited response.

Yamaha team says it will not participate in the Qatar Grand Prix motorcycle race due to the "Middle East situation." The Japanese company announced it will not travel to Doha for the MotoGP race scheduled from November 15 to 17 at the Lusail International Circuit. The event organizer criticized Yamaha's decision as "disappointing."
A group of families applying for youth population land protested, saying "They made a law, we had children, but now they do not give the land."

Simultaneously with Mojtaba Khamenei's order to remove geographical restrictions of the war, Trump spoke about his intention to attack the nuclear facilities at Kuh-e-Kalang, and the New York Post reported, quoting a former Mossad deputy, that Israel is seeking to eliminate the leaders of the Islamic Republic, especially four individuals, in the upcoming war.
Kumar Royan and Sadruddin Esmaeilzadeh, two citizens from Oshnavieh, were reportedly detained by security forces and transferred to an unknown location.

Abbas Aliabadi, the Minister of Energy, said in a nationwide power outage drill that they recently received a letter from the Imam emphasizing moving towards a direction where homes not only become independent from external power supply but can also sell or transfer their surplus electricity to neighbors. He added that in conditions where an enemy could attack at any moment, they must think about network resilience. He continued that the use of emergency generators has been communicated to them as a fundamental strategy by the Passive Defense Organization, and good actions have been taken in this regard.

Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry called for immediate global action to ensure maritime security and protect international trade following an attack on the Qatari liquefied natural gas ship "Al Maydah" in the Persian Gulf. The ministry strongly condemned the attack and expressed opposition to any action threatening shipping security and global energy supply. Saudi Arabia also announced solidarity with Qatar in all its measures to protect ships and international trade security.

A video sent to Iran International shows a woman performing the royal anthem in front of the National Garden gate in Tehran. The sender said she sang this anthem on the occasion of Prince Reza Pahlavi's birthday.
Iranian media reported that Hamid Alidousti, former player of Iran's national football team and Homa club and technical manager of Chadormalu team, died today Sunday after battling cancer.

Qatar has recently become one of the main mediators between the Islamic Republic and the United States. Attacks by the Islamic Republic on energy facilities and vessels related to Qatar have caused heavy damages to the country. However, Doha insists on its mediating role.

Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition, announced that a ballistic missile and a Houthi drone launched towards southern Saudi Arabia were intercepted and destroyed. Al-Maliki reported in two separate messages on his official X account the destruction of the ballistic missile by air defense and then the interception and destruction of the drone. The exact location of the interception and the possible targets of the missile and drone were not specified.

On the fourth and final day of the World Freestyle Wrestling Championships in Astana, Kazakhstan, Mohammad Nokhodi won the silver medal and Amir Mohammad Yazdani won the bronze medal. Iran ranked third after the United States and Russia. This report is based on the assessment of sports journalist Mehdi Rostampour.

Masoud Pezeshkian said in a government information council meeting that the adjustment of gasoline, electricity, and diesel prices will be done gradually and with planning to use the resulting resources for supplying goods and improving people's livelihoods. He added that if electricity consumption is reduced, significant financial resources will be freed that can be used to increase employees' salaries. Pezeshkian also said that if savings are made in gas, diesel, and gasoline consumption, staff salaries can be increased and their living conditions improved.

Ata Hasanian, an economic and energy journalist, mentioned that officials of the Islamic Republic are worried about the outbreak of war and said that the focus of the authorities is not on the development of the country but on preparing for conditions where energy infrastructure might be damaged and access to electricity, gas, gasoline, and diesel could be disrupted.
Videos sent to Iran International show that a group of Iranians living in the UK gathered in Newcastle on Saturday, 9 Aban, to commemorate Cyrus Day and shouted "Death to the Islamic Republic."

Jack Keane, former vice chairman of the US Joint Chiefs of Staff, said economic pressure alone is not enough to confront the Islamic Republic and the US and its allies must put this regime "on the path to real collapse." He responded to Mojtaba Khamenei's threat about unlimited geographic retaliation by saying the Islamic Republic will retaliate if attacked, but these threats will not deter Trump and Netanyahu from their decision. Keane added that Tehran's threats have affected Gulf countries, which have previously asked Trump not to attack.

Hosseinali Haji Deligani, deputy chairman of the Article 90 Commission of the Parliament, said the resistance front has adopted a new strategy in military and security dimensions and enjoys the support of nations. He added that it is necessary for all nations of the region to join the resistance movement and connect their governments to this movement. Haji Deligani also said the Islamic Republic has proven its position as the main supporter of the Islamic community through steadfastness on the field.

Three death row prisoners in the counties of Shirvan, Pakdasht, and a city in Fars province were spared from execution due to the forgiveness of the victims' families. The head of the Dispute Resolution Center reported reconciliation in over 800 death penalty cases in the past year.

Khatun Bam, Iran's women's football representative in the AFC Women's Champions League, lost 4-1 in their first match against the Japanese representative. Report by Raha Pourbakhsh, Iran International.

Gulf countries' efforts to prevent the resumption of war have increased. The leaders of these countries, who have borne the main burden of retaliatory attacks by the Islamic Republic due to hosting US bases, are calling for de-escalation. It is expected that in a potential round of US and Israeli attacks, in addition to nuclear and military targets, Iran's civilian infrastructure will also be targeted.

Political analyst Nejat Bahrami, referring to the recent stances of Islamic Republic officials and the increased US military presence in the region, said that signs indicate an imminent failure of diplomacy. According to him, Donald Trump's recent statements, unlike in previous months, also show no hope for negotiations.

At least seven protest gatherings of Social Security and Steel retirees were held in the cities of Shush, Ahvaz, Kermanshah, Tehran, Dezful, and Rasht. The retirees demanded improvement in living conditions, salary increases, and free medical and social services. Additionally, some steel retirees in Isfahan protested against the performance of the supplementary insurance "Dana," medical problems, and incomplete implementation of salary adjustments.

Kolbari in Kurdish areas, fuel carrying in Baluchistan, and other hazardous informal jobs in border regions are part of the economic reality of areas facing structural poverty and deprivation. Local residents in places like Azerbaijan complain about environmental pollution and limited shares of mining profits, sometimes working in unsafe mines or being shot at by security forces on mining routes. This situation reflects weaknesses in economic and development policies and the need to examine the government's responsibility for the lives of those who engage in these activities to earn a living.

According to videos received by Iran International, a group of Iranians living in Germany gathered in Hamburg on Saturday, 9 Aban, to protest against the executions by the Islamic Republic, shouting "By the blood of comrades, we stand until the end."

The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) has received a report of an incident in the Strait of Hormuz. The captain of a commercial ship transmitted a Mayday emergency message stating that another ship was targeted by an unknown projectile.
A citizen in Markazi province was arrested by the IRGC forces on charges of spying for Israel. A video of this citizen's confession has been released, but the conditions of its recording are unclear.

Excelsior Rotterdam football team lost 9-0 to Twente in the eleventh week of the Dutch Eredivisie. Alireza Jahanbakhsh, captain of the Iranian national team, was on the bench in this match. Excelsior finished the match without a single shot after Nesto Chron was sent off in the fifth minute and is ranked 16th in the league table.

Axios reported that Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel, has asked Donald Trump, President of the United States, to attack Iran immediately after the midterm elections, but Trump currently wants to give negotiations a chance. Trump and Netanyahu spoke on the phone on Saturday, 9 Aban, about the status of negotiations and the timing of resuming military operations. Trump is pursuing two paths simultaneously: trying to reach an agreement to resume direct negotiations and preparing for the possibility of returning to extensive military operations after the elections.

The death sentence of Arman Marefati, one of the detainees of the January 1404 protests, was confirmed by the Supreme Court. He had previously been sentenced to death by Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. The sentence was issued on charges including participation in operational actions against national security and setting fire to a mosque and seminary.

Three detainees from the December 1404 protests in Mashhad, including 23-year-old Matin Farnian, were sentenced to death by the Fifth Branch of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court on charges of "waging war against God". These individuals are currently imprisoned in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. This was reported by the HRANA news agency.

The Telegram channel "Tehran-Student" reported that Shahin Shokoohi, a sociology PhD student at the University of Tehran, self-immolated on Sunday, 10 Aban, in front of the Foolad building of the university. This student had been summoned multiple times to the university disciplinary committee and was under security pressures from outside institutions. After the self-immolation, he was transferred to a medical center but no information about his health status has been released, and there is a possibility of his arrest.

Manouchehr Motaki, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said about the message attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei that the removal of the "geographical limitation" means the future war will no longer be regional and can extend beyond the region. He added that European countries that provide their bases to American fighter jets are considered "partners" in the attacks.

The United States is on the verge of midterm elections, held every two years, which change the composition of the House of Representatives and part of the Senate. This cycle, the costs of the war with the Islamic Republic and rising fuel and goods prices have become key points of competition. Report by Samira Ghoraei, Iran International reporter.

The Harana website reported that three detainees of the Iranian National Revolution in Dey 1404 in Mashhad were sentenced to death on charges of "enmity against God" in a joint case. The sentence for these three was issued in the fifth branch of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court headed by Hossein Yazdankhah. These three were arrested by security forces in Mashhad on the 29th and 30th of Dey 1404.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said on the program "Cheshmandaz" that statistics can be misleading and that inflation and purchasing power are different issues. He stated that one million students did not attend school due to lack of money and that Iran's economic infrastructure has been damaged after the war. Mahdavi-Azad warned that if officials do not compromise and the situation does not change, they themselves say that we will face a death tsunami.

Leila Morvati, a political analyst, said that the continuation of indirect negotiations and disagreements over the nuclear program, lifting sanctions, and releasing frozen assets have made reaching an agreement difficult. According to her, given the insistence of both sides on their positions and the escalation of military threats, it is unlikely that the negotiations will yield results in the short term unless one side retreats from some of its demands.

Mohammad Qaedi said no country has full control over the Strait of Hormuz, and the US is militarily superior, but the Islamic Republic can disrupt passage with missiles, drones, and naval mines. He added that Qatar and GCC countries' reactions to the attack on a Qatari ship do not necessarily mean readiness for military action. Qaedi also said continued attacks could complicate Qatar's mediation between Tehran and Washington and increase internal disputes within the Islamic Republic.

Donald Trump, at a campaign rally in Iowa, said he had a very good conversation with the Israeli Prime Minister. He confirmed that he also spoke about Iran. Earlier reports indicated the call was about Washington's negotiations with Iran and the possibility of military action.

A private jet of model "Learjet 60" crashed in a mobile home community in Palm Beach, Florida, destroying at least one residential pre-fabricated house and causing a severe fire. Rescue and fire officials have confirmed "multiple casualties" but the exact numbers are not yet known. The flight was from Austin International Airport in Texas to the Bahamas and crashed after a sudden right deviation from about 8,000 feet at high speed.

Morad Veysi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that from Wednesday, after the end of the US Congress elections, we will likely face a different Trump who is no longer worried about the impact of war on the election results and does not need the American people's vote for re-election. He added that if no agreement is reached with the Islamic Republic, Trump will have more freedom in the remaining two years of his presidency to intensify economic pressure, oil blockade, and even military attacks. Veysi asked whether Wednesday will mark the beginning of a new phase of confrontation between the US and the Islamic Republic and whether Trump is moving towards a bigger war.

Morad Veysi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that free education in Iran, which was a product of the Shah's era, has completely disappeared. He added that schools charge parents money at registration, during the school year, and even when giving report cards. He also said that the milk quota for schools has been cut for one year, but an amount equivalent to three and a half times the school milk budget has been paid to Hezbollah Lebanon, and now the cost of schools has fallen on the shoulders of parents.

Amir Giti, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said Donald Trump, despite considering a military option against the Islamic Republic, still wants to give diplomacy another chance. He added that the phone conversation between Trump and Netanyahu was described as frank and difficult. Giti emphasized that Washington's main demand is to resolve the Islamic Republic's nuclear issue, and continuing negotiations does not necessarily mean abandoning military action.

Hamid Alidousti, a football player who played for Homa in the 1350s and 1360s and was popular among football fans, died today on 10 Aban 1405. He stayed with Homa while most players were in Taj (Esteghlal) and Persepolis teams. An interview with Mohammad Taghavi and Raha Pourbakhsh about him was conducted on the Hat-trick program.

Moloud Hajizadeh, an economic journalist, said that conditioning people's salary increases on saving electricity and gasoline by Masoud Pezeshkian is a sign of transferring the costs of government inefficiency to society. He added that instead of solving the energy crisis, the government conditions salary payments and service provision on people's savings. Hajizadeh also said about the household self-sufficiency plan in electricity production that the government has not made the necessary investments in recent years and implementing such plans can put more economic pressure on households.

Iranians living in Los Angeles gathered in front of the city's federal building to commemorate Cyrus the Great Day and emphasized the continuation of the Iranian national revolution. Participants also expressed their opposition to the Islamic Republic and their support for Prince Reza Pahlavi. This gathering was held on the occasion of the 7th of Aban, simultaneously with similar gatherings of Iranians in other cities around the world.

Mohammad Taghavi said in the Hattrick program that Mehdi Tartaar has not coached a team competing for the championship so far, and in his opinion, Tartaar needs to gain experience more than the young players of Persepolis.

Manouchehr Mottaki, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said the Islamic Republic has the ability to increase the range of its missiles according to military needs. He added that if the source of a threat is confirmed, Iran can carry out a preemptive attack. The military doctrine of the Islamic Republic also includes an "if necessary" offensive approach.

Russian officials reported a large-scale drone attack causing heavy damage to the Kstovo refinery, one of Russia's largest oil facilities. War monitoring channels reported that Ukraine targeted this refinery.

The Atlantic magazine reported on Sunday, 10 Aban, that Donald Trump sought opinions from his allies about the performance of Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of Defense, and General Dan Keen, the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. Some of Trump's close associates accused Hegseth of presenting an overly optimistic picture of the war situation, a claim the Pentagon denied. Last week, Hegseth and Keen presented military options against the Islamic Republic to Trump and his deputy, and the White House stated Trump has full confidence in both, but no order to resume attacks has been issued yet.

Donald Trump said he protected his country against the world's biggest state sponsor of terrorism. He added that these enemies have attacked the US since 1979 and hundreds of young Americans have been killed. Trump said they have suffered heavy blows and he is trying to find someone to talk to but has not succeeded.

Mehdi Taj, head of the Iranian Football Federation and vice president of the Asian Football Confederation, said the futsal matches have been canceled due to attacks in Saudi Arabia. He added that on November 19, 2026, it will be determined whether the Asian Cup matches will be held, but if conditions remain the same, they probably will not be held. These remarks come as the AFC announced the final schedule for the 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia last week.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations announced that a tanker moving southeast in the Persian Gulf, 72 nautical miles east of Ras Al-Khafji, Saudi Arabia, was hit from the left by two unidentified projectiles. The incident occurred at 23:47 GMT on Sunday, 10 Aban. All tanker crew members are safe and no environmental consequences have been reported so far.

Reuters reported on Monday, November 2, 2026, that three major Chinese airlines recorded net losses in the first nine months of 2026. According to the report, a sharp increase in fuel prices following the Iran war has weakened their profitability outlook. Analysts predict all three companies will end 2026 with a net loss.

The US Central Command, CENTCOM, rejected the Iranian Foreign Minister's claim that Iran does not attack civilians in neighboring countries. CENTCOM stated that Iran has deliberately targeted civilian infrastructure and residential areas in the Gulf countries. The command added that Iran's attacks on civilian mariners have resulted in the deaths of more than 20 people in recent months.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center has received a report of an incident 72 nautical miles east of Ras Al-Khafji, Saudi Arabia. An oil tanker moving southeast in the Persian Gulf was hit on the left side by two unidentified projectiles.

Reza Arab, a political analyst, referring to statements by Mike Huckabee, the US ambassador to Israel, said there is no serious sign of disagreement between Trump and Netanyahu. He pointed to close military cooperation between the US and Israel and said announcing the timing of an attack removes the element of surprise. Arab added that the Islamic Republic's failure to obtain an atomic bomb was not due to a religious fatwa but because Israel and the US prevented its progress, and the desire to acquire nuclear weapons has been part of the Islamic Republic's political goals.

Haaretz reported on Monday, 11 Aban that Israeli military officials said Hamas's military wing is gradually rebuilding its capabilities and weakening the operational achievements of the Israeli army in the Gaza war. Hamas currently has hundreds of rockets and is trying to rebuild its weapons production capacity with smuggling help from inside Israel. The Israeli army, while preparing for a possible resumption of clashes with Iran or Hezbollah, wants to transfer forces stationed in the ongoing operation in Hebron to other areas.

Kamyar Behrang, a member of Iran International's editorial board, referring to Israel's Channel 12 report about the existence of approximately 1,700 Islamic Republic ballistic missiles capable of reaching Israel, said that this statistic indicates a missile reserve and does not, by itself, show the immediate launch capability. He added that the loss of some missile sites and launch systems had reduced the Islamic Republic's simultaneous firing capability in the final days of previous wars. Behrang also said that threatening Arab countries pushes them towards greater defense cooperation with the US and Israel, and the Islamic Republic's threat of a preemptive strike could give the US and Israel the upper hand for earlier action against the Islamic Republic.

Iranians residing in Canada gathered to protest a joint statement by the Canadian government and the United Arab Emirates regarding the three Iranian islands. This statement was issued after the Canadian Prime Minister's meeting with the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, identifying Abu Musa, Greater Tunb, and Lesser Tunb islands as belonging to the UAE. Protesters emphasized Iran's sovereignty over these islands and the preservation of the country's territorial integrity, with a consultant for the Iran Prosperity Project calling on the Canadian Prime Minister to amend the statement.

Hossein Shariatmadari, editor-in-chief of Kayhan newspaper, wrote that the US insists that the nuclear program also be part of the negotiations with Washington through a Qatari mediator, with the greatest emphasis on diluting 400 kilograms of 60% uranium in Iran or a third country, and allowing inspections of the Islamic Republic's nuclear facilities. Shariatmadari wrote on Monday, November 2, 2026, that Islamic Republic officials have decisively rejected this "deceptive plan" and emphasized the fulfillment of their seven proposed conditions. He added that by raising the nuclear condition, the US intends to create a justifiable reason for a failed attack on Iran.
